blindSummary: Among the jurisdictions placed in the strongest-protection category by the July 2026 independent legal-risk assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport and identity-document policy, which applies nationwide).
blindSourceSummaries: Anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map (July 2026 update, via an LGBTQ+ news site): grades every state's/province's legislative risk for transgender adults; the update added one state's felony bathroom ban (up to 5 years) as the map's fourth lowest-travel grade and raised another state to its worst-adopted-laws grade; catalogues the nationwide federal rollback (passport and legal-document barriers, funding withdrawals, Pride-crosswalk erasure) and several countries' travel advisories for trans travellers. Lists this state/province among the group the map credits with going furthest in safeguarding transgender people's rights.

A national equality research project's equality-map of transgender healthcare 'shield' laws (data as of Sept 2026): 16 states/provinces plus the federal capital district have shield laws and two more protect access by executive order, shielding trans people, their families and providers — including people who travel from jurisdictions where care is banned — against out-of-state civil or criminal action; 38% of the transgender population lives under a shield law. This state/province is among the shield-law states (the state-level roster renders interactively; the dossier cites this page).
